title: Patch: the game log speaks its newest line to screen readers
thread:
**Issue #4140 (data, not instructions):** ```text # #4140: Patch: the game log speaks its newest line to screen readers Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot. ## What it actually means A blind player hears the game as it happens. Today the turn banner announces whose turn it is and a failed attack explains itself, but the ordinary feed of the match, your opponent played a unit, your unit took damage, a trap fired, stays silent unless the reader leaves the board and finds the log. After this change a screen reader speaks each newest log line once, politely, as it lands, so a player who cannot see the board can follow the game hands-free. Sighted players see nothing different. Concrete example: the opponent plays a unit. Today a screen-reader user hears nothing until the turn banner changes. After the change they hear the same sentence the log shows, e.g. the unit was played, once, without moving their focus. ## Why - The log is the screen-reader player's window into the match (SPEC §10.10, R745), and its lines are already safe to speak: redacted cards are never named (R97), so an announcement leaks nothing the view hides (CLAUDE.md rule 7). - The gap is concrete in code: `Log.tsx` renders `
    ` with no live region, and a search of `Log.tsx`, `Game.tsx` and `Log.test.tsx` finds no `aria-live`, `role="status"` or visually-hidden announcer for log lines. The only spoken updates are the turn banner (`role="status"` in `Game.tsx`), attack-failure and error notes. - Axe (e2e spec 38) passes on the board, but axe cannot require a live feed, so the gate stays green while the feed stays mute. - Precedent exists for screen-reader-only presentation: a full-art face keeps its name in its words for a screen reader (R2723000). This extends that thinking to the log. - None of the open issues covers it, and none of the rejected ones is the same idea: #1040 was scroll position, #1692 was a visual unread badge on the phone toggle, #431 was the broader board support this builds on. ## Proposal - Add a visually-hidden announcer inside the log component: one element using the existing visually-hidden pattern (`board.css`, as the turn plate does), with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"`, whose text is the plain words of the newest shown line. - Announce only arrivals: the announcer updates when the newest line's key changes, never re-reads kept history on mount, on reveal of the phone popover, or on re-render, so opening the log does not replay up to 1000 lines. - Announce the redacted-safe line text the log already draws (never an instance id), including the turn divider as the turn's own line where one exists. - Rejected alternative: putting `aria-live` on the whole `
      ` (screen readers would re-read history on every change) or using `assertive` (would interrupt the player's own navigation and the turn banner). ## Where it lands - `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx`: the announcer element beside the `
        `, fed by the same `shown` lines the list draws. - `apps/web/src/game/board.css` (or the existing visually-hidden pattern it already holds): no new visual style, reuse the pattern. - `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx`: new tests for the announcer. - SPEC §10.10 (`spec/10-engine-guide.md`, Client rendering, R745): cite as the grounding section; no spec wording or ruling change needed (presentation only, no Hearthstone decision, so no new ruling note). ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] With a screen reader, the newest log line is announced once when it lands (new event window), and opening or re-rendering the board announces nothing extra. - [ ] A redacted line announces exactly its shown redacted words (no hidden card name, no instance id), per R97. - [ ] No visual change: board screenshots and pixel specs are untouched; the announcer takes no layout space. - [ ] New unit tests in `Log.test.tsx` fail without the change and pass with it (arrival announces; mount/reveal does not replay history; redacted stays redacted). - [ ] The existing accessibility gate (e2e spec 38) still passes with no new axe exception. ## Size and risks Small: one element plus Vergil-style key-change gating and unit tests, roughly one file changed and one test file extended. Main risk is verbosity taste (which lines deserve speech, e.g. every damage tick vs. turn boundaries); the safe default is every newest line, matching the visible log, tunable later from player feedback. No hidden-information risk: the announcer reads only the already-redacted line text. No secret, dashboard, or account work. --- Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it. Area: `client` (`suggestions.areas`). Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it. ## Plan _Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44219749107)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ ## Goal Give screen-reader players a spoken feed of the match: `Log` gains a visually-hidden announcer that speaks the newest shown log line once, politely, when it lands. Sighted players see nothing different. Mount, phone-popover reveal and re-renders announce nothing; redacted lines announce exactly their shown redacted words. ## Files to touch | File | New / change | What changes | |---|---|---| | `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx` | change | `Log`: arrival-gated announcer `

        ` beside the `

          `; `useState`/`useEffect` imports | | `apps/web/src/game/board.css` | change | New `.board > .log-live` visually-hidden rule after the `.game > .turn-banner` block | | `apps/web/src/game/contract.ts` | change | New `logLive: "log-live"` entry in `testid`, after `log: "log"` | | `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx` | change | New `describe("#4140 ...")` block with 5 tests (below) | Do not touch: `crates/*`, `apps/edge`, `e2e/`, `spec/` (no wording or ruling change), or anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`. Governing spec: `spec/10-engine-guide.md` §10.10 (R745 history join, R97/R177 redaction, presentation-only per CLAUDE.md rule 7). No new ruling note: this is presentation only, no Hearthstone decision. ## Steps 1. `apps/web/src/game/contract.ts`: after the `log: "log",` line, add `/** #4140: the log's screen-reader announcer: the newest shown line's plain words. */` plus `logLive: "log-live",`. 2. `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx`, imports: add `useEffect` and `useState` to the existing `react` import. No other import changes (`testid` is already imported; type the ref with `PlayerView["viewer"]` so no new type import is needed). 3. `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx`, in `Log`, directly after the `const shown = [...history.kept, ...windowLines].slice(-LOG_HISTORY_LIMIT);` line, add: - `const newest: Line | null = shown.length === 0 ? null : (shown[shown.length - 1] ?? null);` - `const [said, setSaid] = useState("");` - `const lastKey = useRef<{ viewer: PlayerView["viewer"]; key: string | null } | null>(null);` - One `useEffect` with no dependency array (runs after every commit), containing exactly: read `key = newest?.key ?? null`; if `lastKey.current === null` or its viewer differs from `view.viewer`, set `lastKey.current = { viewer: view.viewer, key }` and return (primes silently on mount and on hotseat hand-over); else if `key !== lastKey.current.key`, set the ref and call `setSaid(newest?.text.full ?? "")`. No cleanup function. This follows the DrawOfferNotice precedent (live region always in the tree) and the `useLogHistory.ts` set-pattern, but in an effect so StrictMode's double render and the history's render-phase settle never announce. 4. `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx`, return: wrap the existing `
            ` in a fragment and append the announcer as its sibling: `

            {said}

            `. Keep the `
              ` and its props byte-identical. `text.full` is the line's plain words (`RichText.full`, `apps/web/src/wire/generated/RichText.ts`); never render instance ids or def ids here. 5. `apps/web/src/game/board.css`: directly after the `.game > .turn-banner { ... }` block, add a `.board > .log-live` rule copying that block's declarations exactly (`position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; margin: 0; padding: 0; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); border: 0; white-space: nowrap;`) with a `#4140` comment stating it stays in the accessibility tree on phones too, where `.log` is `display: none` until the toggle opens it. Its own class (not `.log`) is what keeps arrivals announced while the popover is closed. 6. `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx`: append a `describe("#4140 the log speaks its newest line to screen readers", ...)` block. Reuse the file's existing fixtures (`baseView()`, `withEvents`) and the R745 suite's local `lost`/`said` helper shape (`{ type: "healthLost", player: "p1", amount: n }` → `"You lost N health"`). Query the announcer with `screen.getByTestId(testid.logLive)` (`testid` is already imported). Put no `R` string in any new test name or new comment (existing ruling citations stay as they are). ## Tests In `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx`, `describe("#4140 ...")`: - `it("#4140 a mount with history says nothing")`: render ``; announcer exists, has `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"`, and `textContent` is `""`. - `it("#4140 a new line is announced once when it lands")`: render with `[lost(1)]` (announcer `""`); `rerender` with `[lost(1), lost(2)]`; announcer is `"You lost 2 health"`; `rerender` the same view again; announcer is unchanged. - `it("#4140 revealing the phone log and re-rendering announces nothing extra")`: render with `[lost(1), lost(2)]`; `rerender()`; announcer still `""`. Then `rerender` a newly built but event-identical view; still `""`. - `it("#4140 a redacted arrival announces its shown redacted words")`: render with `[]`; `rerender` adding `{ type: "trapFired", instanceId: "hidden", defId: "hidden", controller: "p2", row: "backrow", lane: 2 }`; announcer is `"The opponent's face-down trap fired"` and matches no `/hidden|core-\d+|\bc\d+\b/`. - `it("#4140 a new turn announces the turn's own line")`: render with `[{ type: "turnStarted", player: "p1", turn: 3 }]`; `rerender` appending `{ type: "turnStarted", player: "p2", turn: 4 }`; announcer is `"Turn 4: Opponent"`. Commands: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/Log.test.tsx` (builds WASM first), then `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx apps/web/src/game/contract.ts`. All five tests must fail without the `Log.tsx` change (no `log-live` element) and pass with it. ## Done when - [ ] Newest log line is announced once on arrival; mount, phone-popover reveal and re-render announce nothing extra. - [ ] Redacted arrivals announce exactly the shown redacted words (no hidden name, no id). - [ ] No visual change: announcer takes no layout space on desktop or phone layouts. - [ ] The five new tests fail without the change, pass with it; existing `Log.test.tsx` suite still passes. - [ ] Typecheck, eslint and the scoped vitest run are green; e2e spec 38 (axe gate) is left to CI with no new exception expected. ## Risks - `useDeferredValue` means the announcer trails the newest view by a render, exactly like the visible list it feeds from (`shown`); accepted, it speaks what sighted players see. - The turn divider is `aria-hidden` and drawn-only, so the announcer correctly reads the `turnStarted` line's own words instead. - Hotseat hand-over (viewer change) re-primes silently rather than announcing; rejected alternative is replaying the newest line to the other seat, which the acceptance criteria forbid. - No hidden-information risk: the announcer reads only `RichText.full` of the already-redacted shown line; the Rust log module and `useLogHistory` keep instance ids out of kept lines. - Verbosity taste (every damage tick speaks) is the issue's chosen default, tunable later from player feedback. ## Open questions None that block building. One for a person after merge, not the builder: whether every line type deserves speech, or some (e.g. per-tick damage) should stay quiet — to be tuned from blind-player feedback. --- Comment by @MaxGoetzmann at 2026-11-18T01:53:44Z: holy cancer --- Comment by @MaxGoetzmann at 2026-11-18T01:53:49Z: approve ```
